title: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026’s Real World AI Stage features robots, automated factories, and extinct animals
author: Modelverse Editorial
excerpt: On our new Real World AI stage, we’ll be focusing on the intersection between the digital and physical, and all the ways we’ll continue to see a blending of the two.
body:
## Expansion of AI Stages at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
The upcoming TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 event is set to feature an expanded AI presence, with not one, but two dedicated stages. The traditional AI Stage will continue to showcase the latest developments and innovations in the field, while the newly introduced Real World AI Stage will focus on the intersection of digital and physical technologies.

## Focus on Real-World Applications
The Real World AI Stage will explore the various ways in which autonomous hardware is being integrated into public spaces, homes, and even conservation efforts, such as bringing back extinct species. The stage will host speakers from prominent companies like Shield AI, Colossal Biosciences, and FieldAI, among others. The discussions will delve into the challenges and consequences of deploying AI systems in the physical world, where mistakes can have significant real-world implications.

## Implications for Developers and Researchers
The Real World AI Stage lineup will tackle tough questions, such as determining when an autonomous system is ready for safe deployment. This is a critical concern for developers and researchers working on hard tech projects, including autonomous vehicles, defense technologies, and industrial systems. By exploring these issues and showcasing the latest advancements, the Real World AI Stage aims to provide valuable insights and inspiration for attendees, who can join the event from October 13 to 15 at San Francisco's Moscone West.
